page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.16xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ecs.ic5 family. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the weak category, while single-threaded gzip compression is poor. Conversely, multi-threaded capabilities are more robust, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the strong category. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU scores all align with average tier results. Memory bandwidth across both small and large blocks also registers in the average range.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.ic5.16xlarge is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:1, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. However, the dedicated CPU allocation and high physical core count provide stable multi-threaded execution. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this hardware profile is optimized for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints or local storage. It is suited for parallel processing workloads, multi-threaded decompression tasks, software compilation, and moderate web serving operations.
